name: Level Two Training of the Virtual Learning Environment Rollout at AKU-SONAM Kenya

content.title: Level Two Training of the Virtual Learning Environment Rollout at AKU-SONAM Kenya
content.summary: The Network of Blended and Digital Learning (BDL) facilitated the level two training of the Virtual Learning Environment Rollout Programme at the School of Nursing and Midwifery (SONAM) in Kenya focused on topics such as effective online pedagogy.

content.text: On the 18th and 19th of January, 2018, the Network of Blended and Digital Learning (BDL) facilitated the level two training of the Virtual Learning Environment Rollout Programme at the School of Nursing and Midwifery (SONAM) in Kenya.

The training focused on topics such as principles of effective online pedagogies, copyright guidelines at AKU, and collaborative learning. The BDL team demonstrated how SONAM faculty can set up an online discussion forum for their courses. They also demonstrated how faculty can perform assessments in the online learning environment by developing quizzes on Moodle. Faculty participated in reflective activities to discuss the
of critical thinking and deliberated on ideas to enhance student learning through online platforms and reflective journals.

The lively discussions that followed highlighted how faculty were able to contextualise student problems and classroom challenges. One faculty member stated that the physical structure of the classroom inhibited discussions in his/her course. Together, the faculty and the BDL team brainstormed ideas to engage students in meaningful discussions through the Moodle platform. Also, a change in perceptions of teaching was noticed among participants as they wished to engage more in collaborative learning. They wanted to create a situation where they teach less but the students still learn more. Faculty wished to play the role of a facilitator than that of a teacher.

Towards the end of the workshop, faculty discussed the way forward and collaboratively generated research ideas. They wished to explore a potential research project focusing on 'The Economic, Social and Environmental Impact of Using Moodle in Teaching and Learning at AKU-SONAM Kenya'. Faculty wished to go beyond implementing online pedagogies and were motivated to explore how these pedagogies impacted their students thus paving way for a culture of evidence based teaching and learning at AKU.
